sentences.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.

sentences.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」

translations.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
translations.idiomatic: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'

sentences.zh: 惠帝乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hui broke off his greeting.

sentences.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。

translations.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
translations.idiomatic: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.

sentences.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。

translations.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."

sentences.zh: 由是奇之。

translations.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」

translations.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
translations.idiomatic: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」

translations.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'
translations.idiomatic: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."

sentences.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。

translations.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.

sentences.zh: 孚雖見尊寵，不以為榮，常有憂色。

translations.literal: Though Fu saw honor and favor he did not regard it as glory and often wore a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: Yet privilege brought him no joy—his face stayed shadowed with worry.

sentences.zh: 臨終，遺令曰：「有魏貞士河內溫縣司馬孚，字叔達，不伊不周，不夷不惠，立身行道，終始若一，當以素棺單槨，斂以時服。」

translations.literal: At his deathbed his testament said, 'There was a Wei loyalist of Henei Wen county, Sima Fu, courtesy Shuda—not acting Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, neither withdrawing like Boyi nor compromising like Liuxiahui—who established himself and walked the Way from first to last as one; bury me in an unvarnished coffin with a single-layer outer shell and dress me in timely ordinary clothes.'
translations.idiomatic: At his deathbed his testament said, 'There was a Wei loyalist of Henei Wen county, Sima Fu, courtesy Shuda—not acting Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, neither withdrawing like Boyi nor compromising like Liuxiahui—who established himself and walked the Way from first to last as one; bury me in an unvarnished coffin with a single-layer outer shell and dress me in timely ordinary clothes.'

sentences.zh: 泰始八年薨，時年九十三。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Taishi at ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Taishi at ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 帝於太極東堂舉哀三日。

translations.literal: The emperor observed mourning three days in the eastern hall of Taiji Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu mourned three days in Taiji's east hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「王勳德超世，尊寵無二，期頤在位，朕之所倚。

translations.literal: An edict said, 'The prince's merit and virtue surpass the age; honor and favor were without peer; he dwelt in office at a hundred years—what I relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, 'The prince's merit and virtue surpass the age; honor and favor were without peer; he dwelt in office at a hundred years—what I relied upon.

sentences.zh: 庶永百齡，諮仰訓導，奄忽殂隕，哀慕感切。

translations.literal: I hoped he would last forever to consult and look up to his instruction—suddenly he has fallen and passed away; grief and longing cut deep.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped he would last forever to consult and look up to his instruction—suddenly he has fallen and passed away; grief and longing cut deep.

sentences.zh: 其以東園溫明秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、緋練百匹、絹布各五百匹、錢百萬，穀千斛以供喪事。

translations.literal: Let there be supplied for the funeral the eastern park warming coffin and secret fittings, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, one hundred bolts of crimson silk, five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, a million cash, and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Let there be supplied for the funeral the eastern park warming coffin and secret fittings, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, one hundred bolts of crimson silk, five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, a million cash, and a thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 諸所施行，皆依漢東平獻王蒼故事。」

translations.literal: All measures implemented shall follow the precedent of Han Prince Xian of Dongping, Liu Cang."
translations.idiomatic: All measures implemented shall follow the precedent of Han Prince Xian of Dongping, Liu Cang."

sentences.zh: 其家遵孚遺旨，所給器物，一不施用。

translations.literal: His family obeyed Fu's testamentary instructions; not one of the supplied implements was used.
translations.idiomatic: The clan honored his will and refused every gifted token.

sentences.zh: 帝再臨喪，親拜盡哀。

translations.literal: The emperor twice attended the mourning and personally bowed in full grief.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan returned twice to bow in deepest sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及葬，又幸都亭，望柩而拜，哀動左右。

translations.literal: When it came to burial he also went to the courier station, gazed toward the bier and bowed, moving those around him to grief.
translations.idiomatic: At interment he halted at the post station, bowed toward the catafalque, and moved every witness.

sentences.zh: 給鑾輅輕車，介士武賁百人，吉凶導從二千餘人，前後鼓吹，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: There were provided imperial escort carriages and light wagons, one hundred armored guards and palace runners, over two thousand attendants for auspicious and inauspicious processions, front and rear trumpets and drums, and joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The cortège drew imperial hearses, a hundred household guards, two thousand ushers, full musical escort, and enshrinement beside the royal ancestors.

sentences.zh: 九子：邕、望、輔、翼、晃、瑰、珪、衡、景。

translations.literal: Nine sons: Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui (lapis), Gui (jade tablet), Heng, Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons named Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui, Gui, Heng, and Jing—the fifth and sixth homophonous but written with different graphs.

sentences.zh: 敬王恬，字元愉，少拜散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、黃門郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Tian courtesy Yuanyu youth appointed irregular cavalry gentleman progressively irregular cavalry attendant yellow-gate gentleman palace Assistant chief.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tian rose through palace attendant posts to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 值海西廢，簡文帝登阼，未解嚴，大司馬桓溫屯中堂，吹警角，恬奏劾溫大不敬，請科罪。

translations.literal: When Haixi was deposed Emperor Jianwen ascended throne martial law not yet lifted Grand Marshal Huan Wen encamped Central Hall sounding alarm horns Tian memorialized impeaching Wen greatly irreverent requesting sentencing crime.
translations.idiomatic: Before demobilization Tian impeached Huan Wen's trumpet fanfare as lèse-majesté.

sentences.zh: 溫視奏歎曰：「此兒乃敢彈我，真可畏也。」

translations.literal: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'
translations.idiomatic: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'

sentences.zh: 吳將施績寇江夏，邊境騷動。

translations.literal: Wu general Shi Ji raided Jiangxia and the border was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu general Shi Ji's strike on Jiangxia threw the frontier into alarm.

sentences.zh: 以望統中軍步騎二萬，出屯龍陂，為二方重鎮，假節，加大都督諸軍事。

translations.literal: Wang was ordered to command twenty thousand infantry and cavalry of the central army, go out and encamp at Longpi as heavy garrison for two fronts, given credentials, and additionally promoted grand commander of all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang led twenty thousand central troops to Longpi as the brace between two theaters, credentials in hand as grand commander.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史胡烈距績，破之，望乃班師。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie resisted Ji and defeated him; thereupon Wang withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing inspector Hu Lie routed Shi Ji, Wang stood down his army.

sentences.zh: 俄而吳將丁奉寇芍陂，望又率諸軍以赴之，未至而奉退。

translations.literal: Soon Wu general Ding Feng raided Quepi; Wang again led the various armies to hurry there; before he arrived Feng withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng's raid on Quepi drew Wang east again, though the enemy slipped away before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 拜大司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 孫皓率眾向壽春，詔望統中軍二萬，騎三千，據淮北。

translations.literal: Sun Hao led a host toward Shouchun; an edict ordered Wang to command twenty thousand central troops and three thousand cavalry and hold north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's thrust toward Shouchun sent Wang to the north bank of the Huai with twenty thousand foot and three thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 皓退，軍罷。

translations.literal: Hao withdrew and the army was disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao withdrew and the mobilization ended.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年薨，時年六十七，賻贈有加，望性儉吝而好聚斂，身亡之後，金帛盈溢，以此獲譏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi, he died at age sixty-seven; funeral gifts were generous in addition; Wang's nature was frugal and stingy yet fond of amassing; after his death gold and silk overflowed; on this account he incurred ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taishi, he died at sixty-seven amid lavish obsequies yet earned ridicule for having hoarded treasure despite a miserly reputation.

sentences.zh: 四子：弈、洪、整、楙。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yi, Hong, Zheng, Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons survived him: Yi, Hong, Zheng, and Mao.

sentences.zh: 河間平王洪，字孔業，出繼叔父昌武亭侯遺。

translations.literal: Prince Ping of Hejian, Hong, courtesy Kongye, went out to succeed uncle Marquis of Changwu precinct Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Hong, Prince Ping of Hejian, styled Kongye, was adopted into uncle Yi's Changwu ting line.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，歷位典農中郎將、原武太守，封襄賁男。

translations.literal: Serving Wei he successively held Agrarian Commandant, governor of Yuanwu, and was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he served as agrarian colonel, Yuanwu governor, and baron of Xiangben.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封河間王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne Hong became prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 立十二年，咸寧二年薨。

translations.literal: After twelve years in the position, he died in Xianning year two.
translations.idiomatic: After twelve years in the position, he died in Xianning year two.

sentences.zh: 二子：威、混。

translations.literal: Two sons: Wei and Hun.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Wei and Hun.

sentences.zh: 威嗣，徙封章武。

translations.literal: Wei succeeded and was transferred enfeoffment to Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei inherited and moved the fief to Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 其後威既繼義陽王望，更立混為洪嗣。

translations.literal: Later when Wei had succeeded Prince of Yiyang Wang, Hun was further established as Hong's successor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei continued Sima Wang's Yiyang title, Hun was designated Hong's heir.

sentences.zh: 混歷位散常侍，薨。

translations.literal: Hun successively held irregular attendant posts and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hun served as supernumerary cavalry attendant and died.
